title: Matchup grid: the fastest and slowest pairings in the league
headline_insight: Pooled over three seasons and 870 team pairings, Atlanta versus Indiana is the highest-scoring matchup at a mean of 255.7 combined points over 10 meetings, while Charlotte versus Portland is the lowest at 197.0 -- a 58-point gap between the league's fastest and slowest recurring games.
what_it_means: Every game is reduced to two team-point totals and pooled by pairing to describe how much scoring each recurring matchup has actually produced. The spread is large: an ATL-IND game has averaged nearly 60 more combined points than a CHA-POR game, a real stylistic signature of who plays fast and loose versus slow and grinding. This describes games already played -- it is not a forecast of any future meeting.
how_to_read: Each pairing's mean_total is the combined-points average over its meetings and mean_margin is the row-minus-column point differential (pooled home and away, not a venue split); pairings need at least 2 meetings to appear.
why_it_matters: It is a compact, honest descriptor of matchup-level scoring texture -- useful context for a totals model, explicitly labeled as history rather than prediction.
caveat: DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY: NOT a prediction of any future matchup, NOT a home/away split (the per-player table carries no venue flag), and pooled across the 2023-24 to 2025-26 seasons.
